The useful conclusion is that a no-spill corrected-K2 16-static-WMMA surface is possible in HIP C++, but this looped spelling does not reproduce RADV throughput; the dynamic loop/control/wait structure and remaining 64-store output contract are still inferior to the oracle. The next Q6 medium attempt should keep the reduced static live surface while targeting RADV's writeback/store topology and outstanding-load behavior.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 RING96 K2 pair-column copy-A+B probe tested the next bounded fragment-sharing axis after full corrected K2 spilled and streamed K2 removed spills but became load/wait bound. It keeps corrected matching-K subtile accumulation while holding two B column fragments at a time and reusing each A fragment across the two column subfragments. The first source spelling selected the intended provider but failed focused p33 CPU-reference with small finite ERR around 0.125 due to reusing one copied A fragment across two WMMA calls. Moving A-fragment materialization per WMMA use fixed correctness. The final CMake/Ninja-built HSACO is resource-clean: wave64, LDS=11264, SGPR=65, VGPR=191, private_segment=0, vgpr_spill_count=0, 32 visible WMMA, 96 ds_load-class instructions, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 43 waitcnt-class instructions. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output with route traces selecting this provider for all three rows. Reject for production performance before model tests. Same-runner focused timing is slower than the accepted VK64 default: total 14118.384 -> 23211.937 us, Vcur 397.662 -> 493.075 us, ffn_out 2424.300 -> 2866.525 us, and result_output 11296.422 -> 19852.338 us. Keep opt-in only. The useful conclusion is that corrected K2 ownership with partial fragment sharing can reduce LDS load traffic from the streamed probe without spills, but the 32-WMMA/64-store shape is still not the RADV medium schedule; the next Q6 medium attempt needs a true 16-WMMA/48-load/96-store lane/writeback contract.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 RING96 K2 streamed copy-A+B probe isolates the pressure axis after the correctness-clean but spill-bound K2 copy-A+B route. It keeps corrected matching-K subtile accumulation, but streams one output column-fragment group at a time: two B fragments remain live across four row fragments while A fragments are loaded on demand. This preserves the single-wave BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64 and 11264-byte LDS footprint and removes the K2 spill cliff: CMake/Ninja-built HSACO reports SGPR=65, VGPR=175, private_segment=0, and vgpr_spill_count=0. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output with route traces selecting this provider for all three rows. Reject for production performance before model tests. The no-spill tradeoff increases LDS traffic and waits: 32 visible WMMA, 160 ds_load-class instructions, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 61 s_waitcnt-class instructions. Same-runner focused timing is slower than the accepted VK64 default: total 14254.969 -> 24640.156 us, Vcur 397.222 -> 545.102 us, ffn_out 2360.844 -> 3041.781 us, and result_output 11496.903 -> 21053.273 us. Keep opt-in only. The useful conclusion is that corrected K2 ownership is now proven and the spill can be removed, but the streamed HIP spelling is load/wait bound; the next Q6 medium attempt needs to share fragments without full-array spilling or per-row reload amplification.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 RING96 K2 copy-A+B probe is the first production-ABI transfer after the cross-reference diagnosis proved old RING96 computed a cross/rotated product. It keeps the single-wave BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64 and 11264-byte LDS footprint, but explicitly accumulates both K subtiles against matching B fragments before the unrotated store. This repairs correctness: focused p33 CPU-reference passed Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output with route traces selecting this provider for all three rows. Reject for production performance before model tests. The CMake/Ninja-built HSACO spills badly: wave64, LDS=11264, SGPR=65, VGPR=256, private_segment=128, and vgpr_spill_count=31, with 32 visible WMMA, 64 ds_load-class instructions, 64 buffer_store_b32, and scratch traffic. Same-runner focused timing is much slower than the accepted VK64 default: total 13988.144 -> 51243.250 us, Vcur 397.181 -> 662.780 us, ffn_out 2368.391 -> 5971.729 us, and result_output 11222.571 -> 44608.740 us. Keep the route opt-in only as useful evidence: the cross-tile math is now fixed, but doubling the K-subtile WMMA work in this HIP spelling causes spills and is not the RADV medium schedule.

The Q6_K VK64 wave4row batch-wait probe transferred the Q5_K batch-wait load-window spelling to the correctness-clean Q6 wave4row route. It preserves BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64, 11264 bytes LDS, four-wave row-stripe ownership, four live accumulators per wave, direct F32 RHS, and raw buffer stores, while issuing each four-B64 fragment read group before one lgkmcnt wait instead of relying on a single post-load wait. It built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under explicit opt-in. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle rejects schedule parity: wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=92, LDS=11264, no spills, 40 ds_load_b64, 36 waitcnt-class ops, and 8 visible WMMA. This preserves the footprint but still misses RADV's 16 WMMA, 48 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 64 ds_store_b16, 96 buffer_store_b32, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=40; the emitted hot window remains only 12 pre-WMMA b64 loads and lgkmcnt=0. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed with route traces selecting this provider for Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output. Same-runner focused timing rejects promotion versus the accepted VK64 default: Q6 focus sum 14300.111 -> 14966.007 us, Vcur 397.506 -> 412.490 us, ffn_out 2233.021 -> 2315.128 us, and result_output 11669.584 -> 12238.390 us. Keep opt-in only. The useful conclusion is that per-fragment batch waits are correct but do not recover the RADV outstanding-load/writeback contract for Q6 p33; the next useful probe needs a different low-level fragment/writeback topology or packed schedule, not another wait-only reshuffle of the 8-WMMA direct route.

The Q6_K VK64 wave4row fast-half buffer-store probe tested the next narrow axis after the correctness-clean but slow wave4row route: preserve all-wave low-live row-stripe ownership and single A/B staging, then add selected-half ds_write_b16/ds_read_u16_d16 writeback while reusing the A LDS allocation after the K loop. It built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under explicit opt-in. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle showed the intended partial movement without an LDS cliff: wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=93, LDS=11264, no spills, ds_load_u16_d16=32, ds_store_b16=34, buffer_store_b32=16, and 8 WMMA. This preserves the medium LDS footprint and adds halfword writeback versus plain wave4row, but still remains far from RADV's 16 WMMA, 48 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 64 ds_store_b16, 96 buffer_store_b32, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=40. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed with route traces selecting this provider for Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output. Same-runner focused timing rejects promotion: Q6 focus sum 14027.611 -> 15555.615 us, Vcur 397.715 -> 455.538 us, ffn_out 2244.604 -> 2350.778 us, and result_output 11385.292 -> 12749.299 us. Keep opt-in only. The useful conclusion is that selected-half LDS writeback can be added to wave4row without extra LDS or correctness loss, but it does not fix the p33 gap; the next Q6 medium attempt needs to recover the 16-WMMA/48-b64 outstanding load window and 96-store contract, not just add halfword writeback to an 8-WMMA direct-F32 schedule.

The Q6_K VK64 wave4row probe tested whether the Q5_K all-wave low-live row-stripe ownership transfer could improve the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 medium regime. It keeps BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64 and 11264 bytes LDS, maps each of four wave64 waves to one 16-row stripe, keeps four live accumulators per wave, stages A/B once per K tile, and uses explicit b64 fragment loads plus raw buffer stores. It built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under opt-in. Static comparison against the p33 RADV medium oracle rejects schedule parity before promotion: the selected symbol is wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=92, LDS=11264, no spills, but still only exposes 8 visible v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 versus RADV's 16, 40 ds_load_b64 versus 48, 16 buffer_store_b32 versus 96, 2 ds_store_b16 versus 64, 0 ds_load_u16_d16 versus 64, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0 versus RADV's 40. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed all rows with route traces selecting this provider for Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output. Same-runner focused timing rejects it versus the accepted VK64 default: Q6 focus sum 14392.095 -> 15505.364 us, Vcur 397.828 -> 455.930 us, ffn_out 2237.969 -> 2377.337 us, and result_output 11756.299 -> 12672.097 us. Keep opt-in only. The useful conclusion is that low-live all-wave row ownership is correct for Q6, but it does not recover the RADV medium load/writeback contract or p33 performance; the next Q6 p33 attempt should target grouped outstanding LDS loads plus a compact 96-buffer-store/halfword writeback topology rather than another direct-F32 WMMA ownership reshuffle.

rejections.route: Q6_K packed Q8_1 fallback routes after disabling accepted VK64/VK128 WMMA defaults
rejections.env: GGML_HRX_DISABLE_Q6_K_WMMA16_VK64_PADDED44_W64_F16ACC_WG256_PROMPT=1 and GGML_HRX_DISABLE_Q6_K_WMMA16_VK128_PADDED_W64_F16ACC_WG256_PROMPT=1, optionally with GGML_HRX_ENABLE_Q6_K_Q8_1_X4_MMQ64_PROMPT=1 / GGML_HRX_ENABLE_Q6_K_Q8_1_X4_MMQL128_PROMPT=1 / disable MMQL128/MMQ32 controls
rejections.reason: The current-head Q6 p33 packed fallback audit confirms the accepted VK64 WMMA route remains better overall on the Llama 3.1 odd rows. Disabling VK64/VK128 WMMA and allowing packed policy selected rows2_cols8_wg32 and measured 94127.449 us on the Q6 focus rows versus 14440.438 us for default. Forcing MMQ64 improved only Vcur, 396.587 -> 81.649 us, but regressed ffn_out-0, 2235.143 -> 3291.959 us, and result_output, 11808.708 -> 21521.182 us, for Q6 focus 24894.790 us. Other packed fallbacks were much slower: forced MMQL128 93937.795 us, disable MMQL128 240114.002 us, and disable MMQL128 plus MMQ32 253897.869 us. Keep VK64 as p33 default; the remaining p33 gap needs a new RADV-derived cooperative load/store or lane-ownership source candidate, not a packed-route policy rollback.

A current-head focused HRX/Vulkan refresh on the Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M p33 exported rows showed the largest remaining odd-size gap inside this nominal Q4 row comes from embedded Q6_K rows using the accepted VK64 p33 route: Vcur was 397.261 us versus Vulkan 135.049 us, ffn_out-0 was 2371.184 us versus 857.343 us, and result_output was 11817.773 us versus 8580.169 us. A serial current-head sweep of existing Q6 VK64/WN32/RING96 p33 variants then tested the available route-selectable pivots with CPU-reference first. H4LOAD passed but was only noise-level on the Q6 focus rows, 14308.225 us versus default 14336.825 us, and regressed total focused time, 16243.212 us versus 16187.618 us. WN32, WN32_BUFFERSTORE, and WN32_FAST_HALF passed but were much slower on Q6 focus rows at 20284.283, 20420.293, and 21910.811 us. GROUPK2, GROUPK2_WAIT, RING96, RING96_FAST_HALF, RING96_COPYA, RING96_COPYB, and RING96_COPYAB all failed focused CPU-reference before timing. Keep the accepted VK64 route as the p33 default. The remaining Q6 p33 parity gap is not solved by the existing source-visible VK64/WN32/RING96 catalog variants; the next useful attempt needs a materially different RADV-derived cooperative load/store or lane-ownership primitive.

The current-head packed Q8_0 full-column wave64 repeat confirms the earlier rejection instead of justifying a default route change. A serial focused backend-op sweep over existing packed Q8_0 p512 providers selected the wave64 BN128 split-qsum provider as the best passing route: total 70468.331 us versus 72800.787 us for the default wave32 BN128 split-qsum route, a 1.033x focused speedup, with route traces selecting hrx_mul_mat_vec_q8_0_q8_1_x4_mmq64x128_splitqsum_wave64_wg256_f32 for all five exported rows. Same-binary Llama 3.1 8B Q8_0 p512/fa1 model A/B did not produce stable production evidence: three repeated pairs reported steady wave64/default ratios of 1.006, 1.037, and 1.005, while the first average ratio was slightly negative at 0.995. All runs had zero fallback lines and selected the intended provider under opt-in. This route remains a useful opt-in diagnostic showing the wavefront-mode axis can help the isolated backend-op rows, but the model-level gain is small/noisy and does not address the documented RADV/HIP structural gap. Do not promote this isolated wave64 pivot by default; continue Q8_0 parity work on the Vulkan-oracle schedule deltas, especially cooperative-matrix lane/store ownership and packed dataflow.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 RING96 copy-B and copy-A+B probes completed the route-facing transfer of the standalone fragment-materialization repair. Both built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under explicit opt-in env vars. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle showed both preserve wave64, LDS=11264, no spills, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 48 total ds_load_b64, and 64 buffer_store_b32. Copy-B is the lowest-pressure copy variant at VGPR 175; copy-A+B is VGPR 183; both remain above base RING96 VGPR 163 and RADV medium VGPR 144, and both still miss RADV's halfword/store contract with only 2 ds_store_b16, no ds_load_u16_d16, 64 not 96 buffer stores, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0. Focused p33 CPU-reference rejects both before timing: route traces selected the intended copy-B provider for Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output with finite ERR 33.06, 34.18, and 33.99; copy-A+B selected for the same rows with finite ERR 32.21, 34.98, and 33.56. The standalone fixture repair does not transfer through this real Q6 RING96 catalog ABI. Future Q6 medium work should change the lane/writeback contract or test a different schedule family instead of adding more whole-fragment copies to this route.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 RING96 copy-A probe transferred the smallest standalone fragment-materialization repair from `hrx-hip-bench-coopmat-store-contract` into the real catalog route. It built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under the opt-in env. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle showed one useful movement relative to base RING96: it preserved wave64, LDS=11264, no spills, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, and 48 total ds_load_b64, and the hot window now exposes all 48 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64. The cost is high pressure, VGPR 191 versus base RING96 163 and RADV 144, while the store contract still has only 64 buffer stores, 2 ds_store_b16, no ds_load_u16_d16, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0. Focused p33 CPU-reference rejects it before timing: route traces selected this provider for Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output, but all three failed with finite ERR around 33.1-34.3. The standalone fixture repair does not transfer as A-fragment materialization alone; the next production-directed probe must either test B/A+B materialization or change the lane/writeback contract, not time this route.

The accumulator-direct Q6 VK64/RADV96 fixture closes a hole in the earlier passing coopstore diagnostic. The original `wmma-lds-vk64-radv96` mode computed the compact ring WMMA accumulators but wrote synthetic direct-output values, so it proved the broad opcode/store surface without checking the accumulator lane contract. The new `wmma-lds-vk64-radv96-accdirect` sibling keeps the same CMake/Ninja-built fixture shape and writes computed ring WMMA accumulator groups 0..7 through the direct raw-store path while preserving the staged synthetic groups 8..23. The original control still passes with `bad=0`; the accumulator-direct mode fails immediately and deterministically with `bad=256`, first failure `group=5 slot=0 lane=0`, e.g. actual finite/invalid values such as `-28848` where the expected ring WMMA value is `128`. Reject the RING96 accumulator/lane contract as an unproven production prior. This explains the finite ERR failures in both Q6 RING96 catalog transfers and means the next Q6 p33 probe must first repair or replace the ring WMMA lane ownership in a fixture before another real Q6 catalog route is justified.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 RING96 fast-half buffer-store probe combined the previous RING96 fragment-load schedule with the corrected WN32 fast-half selected/dummy LDS writeback stage. It built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under the opt-in env. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle shows it preserves the useful RING96 math/load surface with wave64, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, and 48 total ds_load_b64, while adding halfword LDS writeback with 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 130 ds_store_b16, 64 buffer_store_b32, and no global stores. It is still not a RADV clone: LDS grows to 15360 bytes versus RADV 11264, VGPR rises to 163 versus RADV 144, buffer_store_b32 is 64 versus RADV 96, halfword LDS traffic overshoots RADV's 64/64 load/store pair, pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 is only 28 versus RADV 48, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt remains 0 versus RADV 40. Focused CPU-reference rejects it before timing: p33 and generated p64 route traces selected this provider for all Q6 rows, but p33 failed with finite ERR around 33.1-33.9 and p64 failed with finite ERR around 2.99-3.00. The useful conclusion is precise: RING96's correctness failure is not fixed by the collision-safe selected-half writeback stage. The remaining issue is in the ring fragment/lane ownership or outstanding-load schedule itself; the next probe should not keep layering post-accumulator staging on this RING96 source.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 WN32/WG128 fast-half buffer-store probe tested the next writeback topology axis after the raw buffer-store rejection: preserve corrected two-wave BM64/BN64 WN32 ownership and raw buffer stores, then stage the selected accumulator half through explicit ds_write_b16/ds_read_u16_d16 with a separate dummy-half LDS tile to avoid lane collisions. The route built through normal CMake/Ninja HSACO generation and selected only under the opt-in env. A first same-source attempt using the Q8 selected-offset trick failed p33 correctness with finite ERR around 1.6 because dummy half placement collided with selected row lanes; the corrected separate-dummy-tile layout passed focused CPU-reference p33 and generated p64 rows with route traces selecting this provider. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle shows useful partial convergence: 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, wave64, no spills, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 66 ds_store_b16, and no global stores. It is still not a RADV schedule clone: LDS grows to 13312 bytes versus RADV 11264, buffer_store_b32 remains 32 versus RADV 96, ds_load_b64 is still emitted as 24 ds_load_2addr_b64 rather than RADV's 48 ds_load_b64, s_waitcnt_depctr is 16 versus RADV 2, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt is 14 versus RADV 40. Same-runner focused timing rejects promotion: default VK64 total 14318.417 us, fast-half buffer-store total 21592.474 us, with baseline/candidate ratios Vcur 0.544, ffn_out 0.702, and result_output 0.660. Keep opt-in only. The useful conclusion is that semantically safe halfword LDS writeback alone increases work and does not close p33; the next probe must combine RADV-like grouped outstanding LDS loads with a compact, non-colliding 96-buffer-store writeback shape rather than adding post-accumulator staging to the current HIP source.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 WN32/WG128 buffer-store probe isolates the first writeback opcode axis after the corrected WN32 route: keep the same two-wave medium tile ownership and direct-F32 RHS math, but switch output writes from global_store_b32 to raw buffer_store_b32. It built through the normal CMake/Ninja HSACO path and selected only under the opt-in env. Static comparison against the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium oracle showed the intended narrow movement, with buffer_store_b32=32 and global_store_b32=0, while preserving 16 WMMA and no spills. It is still far from the RADV contract: RADV has 96 buffer_store_b32, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 64 ds_store_b16, 48 ds_load_b64, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=40; this route has 32 buffer stores, 0 ds_load_u16_d16, 2 ds_store_b16, 0 ds_load_b64, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=10. Focused CPU-reference with route traces passed p33 and generated p64 rows. Same-runner focused timing rejected promotion: default VK64 total 14419.733 us, WN32 buffer-store total 20074.564 us, with baseline/candidate ratios 0.547, 0.674, and 0.736. Raw buffer stores alone are not enough; the next Q6 p33 probe must add the RADV halfword LDS store/load topology and/or grouped outstanding LDS load schedule.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 WN32/WG128 b64asm compile probe tested the next exact static delta from the rejected WN32 route after the WG128 tile-map fix: keep the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 Vulkan medium ownership tuple, but force explicit ds_read_b64 fragment loads through the shared HIP helper. It built through the normal CMake/Ninja HSACO path and is intentionally not wired into runtime selection. Static comparison against the exact RADV medium oracle rejects it before focused correctness or timing: it converts the load opcode class to plain ds_load_b64, but over-serializes the schedule with per-fragment lgkmcnt(0) waits. HSACO emits 128 ds_load_b64 versus RADV 48, 137 s_waitcnt plus 82 s_waitcnt_depctr versus RADV 115 plus 2, only 4 WMMA in the first hot-op window versus RADV 16, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0 versus RADV 40. It also keeps the old writeback surface: 32 global_store_b32, 0 buffer_store_b32, 0 ds_load_u16_d16, and 2 ds_store_b16 versus RADV 96 buffer_store_b32, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, and 64 ds_store_b16. The useful conclusion is that explicit b64 loads are necessary but not sufficient; the next Q6 p33 probe needs grouped/no-wait LDS-load scheduling plus RADV-style halfword/buffer writeback rather than the current per-fragment b64 helper.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 WN32/WG128 probe mechanically tested the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 Vulkan medium ownership tuple: spec=[128,64,64,32,64,32,2,16,16,16,64], two wave64 subgroups per WG128 workgroup, each subgroup owning full 64 rows and 32 columns, yielding 16 WMMA instructions across two K tiles. The shared tile map now derives wave count from HRX_Q6_K_WMMA_VK128_WG_SIZE; without that fix, p33 could pass while masking overlapping col-tile ownership for wider medium rows. It built through the normal CMake/Ninja HSACO path and selected only under the opt-in env. Static comparison against the exact RADV medium oracle confirmed the intended headline surface but rejected schedule parity before model tests because the emitted memory/writeback contract was still unlike RADV: 0 ds_load_b64 versus 48, 0 ds_load_u16_d16 versus 64, 2 ds_store_b16 versus 64, 32 global_store_b32 versus RADV's 96 buffer_store_b32, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=10 versus RADV 40. Focused CPU-reference with route tracing passed p33 and generated p64 rows, proving the corrected WG128 tile map covers the full medium-width tile. Wide/tail non-steal gates with the same opt-in enabled passed p512 and p513 and route logs proved both stayed on the existing VK128 provider. Same-runner focused timing rejected promotion: accepted default VK64 total 14423.157 us, WN32/WG128 total 20129.563 us, with baseline/candidate ratios 0.546, 0.685, and 0.731. Keep the route opt-in only. The useful conclusion is precise: matching Vulkan's two-wave WN32 ownership and WMMA count is not enough; the next Q6 p33 candidate must target the lower-level RADV LDS/load/writeback/wait schedule while preserving correctness.

The Q6_K VK64 RING96 probe ported the passing coopstore-vk64-radv96 diagnostic's compact ring fragment-load shape into the real catalog source behind an opt-in selector. It built through the normal CMake/Ninja HSACO path and partially matched the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium static contract: wave64, LDS=11264, no scratch, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, and 48 ds_load_b64. Reject before timing/model tests. Static comparison still missed the RADV halfword/writeback contract with VGPR=163 versus 144, 0 ds_load_u16_d16 versus 64, 2 ds_store_b16 versus 64, 64 buffer_store_b32 versus 96, only three store clusters, pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 window 28 versus 48, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0 versus RADV 40. Focused p33 CPU-reference with GGML_HRX_TRACE_ROUTES=1 proved this provider selected for Vcur, ffn_out, and result_output, and all three failed with finite ERR around 33-34. The useful evidence is that the production source can hit the 16-WMMA/48-b64 surface; the next Q6 p33 candidate must add the RADV halfword LDS staging/writeback lane ownership instead of only increasing the WMMA issue window.

The no-memory-clobber inline-WMMA probe is a bounded pressure-reduction test against the closest Q8 RADV contract match. It preserves the existing motif192 K2 directwait dataflow, packed A/B LDS staging, 64-lane B64GROUP loads, motif192 halfword LDS writeback, explicit lgkmcnt ladder, and inline v_wmma operand spelling, changing only the artificial `memory` clobber on the inline WMMA instruction. It built through the normal CMake/Ninja HSACO path and was rejected statically before any runtime route gate. Compared with the existing K2 directwait inline-WMMA row, it preserved the same wave64, SGPR=56, VGPR=256, LDS=22528, private_segment=68, 16 VGPR spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 192 LDS reads, 130 LDS writes, 192 VMEM stores, 235 waitcnt-class instructions, and three barriers. The oracle score only moved from `wmma_gap=7` to `wmma_gap=6` because `wmma_in_window` reached 32, while `pre_wmma_ds_load_b64` stayed high at 63 and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt stayed 51. This does not reduce the pressure cliff. Keep the probe as source-level evidence that the spill is not caused by the inline WMMA memory clobber; the next Q8 attempt must reduce the two-K-tile live fragment/accumulator surface or use a lower-level cooperative writeback primitive.

rejections.env: standalone CMake/Ninja-built gfx1151 HIP bench diagnostic; no production selector
rejections.reason: The accparkfull8 standalone diagnostic tested the only credible continuation of the rejected selected-lane accumulator parking path: preserve all eight lanes of the WMMA accumulator vector for the lower eight output groups in LDS, while keeping the upper eight groups resident, so one K traversal and one launch are retained without requiring the impossible full 16-group full-vector LDS footprint. It built through the normal CMake/Ninja hrx-hip-bench-q8-wmma-repro target and was run on exact, odd-column, odd-row, wide, and tail rows: 128x128, 128x129, 129x128, 1024x512, 4096x512, and 4096x513. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=48, VGPR=140, LDS=8192, no spills, 512 v_dot sites, 46 ds_loads, 12 ds_stores, 18 global loads, 64 global stores, 188 s_waitcnts, and 2 barriers. The route selected correctly for p512 and p513, passed focused CPU-reference rows for p512 and p513, and kept exact p33 on the existing MMQ64 route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p513 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 603.45 -> 644.47 us, Qcur 2420.84 -> 2479.59 us, ffn_out 8053.23 -> 8359.72 us, ffn_gate 7682.05 -> 9098.94 us. The explicit ds_read_b64 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the VK128 padded wave64 shape, direct F32 RHS, and ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin while forcing A/B LDS fragment reads through inline assembly. It is rejected for production promotion because focused p512 and p513 CPU-reference rows failed with finite error after optimizer-visible asm: p512 ERR about 0.0058-0.0115 and p513 ERR about 0.0017-0.0115 versus tolerance 0.0005. Earlier no-memory-clobber asm produced NaN/inf, so optimizer visibility matters, but direct half4 asm output, conservative lgkmcnt waits, and explicit address_space(3) base-pointer arithmetic still do not make the forced-b64 fragment feed semantically equivalent to the passing W64 route or RADV. The grouped ds_read_b64 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the VK128 padded wave64 shape and explicit LDS b64 fragment reads, but changed the compute window to load four A fragments and four B fragments for each k-half before issuing the 4x4 WMMA block. A no-wait grouping emitted the same 64 ds_load_b64 class but failed focused p512/p513 correctness with NaNs. The B-oct packed-Q8_1/x4 probe mechanically brackets the only positive post-oracle Q4 packed-path axis. Keep B-quad as the current no-spill default; B-oct exceeds the gfx1151 resource envelope.

The B-half packed-Q8_1/x4 probe is the bounded midpoint between accepted B-quad and rejected B-oct. This tests whether the useful B-oct pre-dot LDS load-window movement can be approximated without carrying the full B window live. It built through normal CMake/Ninja and moved the parsed pre-hot load score from B-quad's 16 toward B-oct at 26, with final pre-hot lgkmcnt 19, but it already hits the same pressure cliff: wave64, SGPR=53, VGPR=192, LDS=8192, private_segment_fixed_size=76, and vgpr_spill_count=18 with scratch load traffic. Reject at the compile/static gate before focused runtime. The B-cache live-window axis is now bracketed: B-quad is the largest no-spill accepted point, B-half spills, and B-oct spills harder.

The B-half-CR packed-Q8_1/x4 probe tested whether CR-major consume order could reduce the B-half live range enough to recover a no-spill schedule while preserving the four-WNITER B-cache preload window, current MMQL128/B-quad dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership. The b64group-bufferstore Q8_0 direct-F32 WMMA probe mechanically combined the strongest source-visible axes after the gfx11 raw-buffer descriptor fix: grouped ds_read_b64 fragment loads, 22528-byte stage allocation, full-tile direct writeback, and raw buffer_store_b32 output. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=195, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 barriers. The focused CPU-reference gates passed for p33, p512, and p513; route traces prove p512/p513 selected the candidate on large rows while p33 stayed on existing narrow packed routes. The Q8_0 B64GROUP dualstage-bufferstore compile-contract probe tested the next exact Vulkan-oracle axis after raw buffer stores plus B64GROUP loads still missed RADV's halfword LDS topology. It preserves the B64GROUP direct-F32 WMMA math/load path and raw buffer_store_b32 output, then uses inline ds_write_b16 and ds_read_u16_d16 to force a duplicated halfword LDS stage while preserving selected-output semantics. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=195, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 130 ds_store_b16, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 34 barriers. The candidate is rejected at the compile-contract gate without runtime because it still fails the RADV large-coopmat contract: RADV has 192 buffer_store_b32, exactly 128 ds_store_b16, only 2 barriers, and VGPR 192. The first-WMMA schedule score adds another rejection reason: RADV has 59 scored pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 events with a final lgkmcnt(51), while this HIP route has only one load immediately before a final lgkmcnt(0), matching the overly conservative wait cadence of the pack-stage control. This proves HIP C++ inline DS can reproduce the halfword LDS read/store opcode class, but the route still lacks RADV's low-barrier cooperative-matrix store/lane ownership, full 192-store writeback, and outstanding LDS-load issue window.

The Q8_0 B64GROUP nowait pack-stage compile-contract probe targeted the first-WMMA issue-window delta directly. The codegen changed, but the first-WMMA score still rejects it as a RADV clone: RADV has 59 scored pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 events and final lgkmcnt(51), while this route has 24 scored pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 events, final lgkmcnt(0), and only 16 WMMA in the scored window. It also still misses RADV's 22528-byte LDS footprint, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, and 192 buffer_store_b32. Reject before runtime; removing helper waits alone is not enough to recover RADV's outstanding LDS-load schedule.

It also still misses RADV's 22528-byte LDS footprint, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, and 192 buffer_store_b32. Reject before runtime; named fragment spelling does not recover the RADV outstanding-load schedule.

The Q8_0 B64GROUP fullpair-bufferstore compile-contract probe tested whether the real direct-WMMA kernel could reproduce RADV's 192-store writeback after the standalone coopmat-store fixture proved HIP C++ can emit that raw store surface. It preserves the B64GROUP direct-F32 WMMA math/load path, 22528-byte LDS allocation, and raw buffer_store_b32 output, then widens only the full-tile buffer-store path to write both accumulator halves while leaving the guarded edge path scalar. The strict RADV contract still fails on ds_load_u16_d16 (128 -> 0), ds_store_b16 (128 -> 2), and VGPR (192 -> 195), so it is rejected before runtime. This narrows the remaining direct-WMMA gap to low-barrier halfword LDS cooperative store/load topology and precise accumulator-lane mapping, not raw buffer store count.

The high-half OPSEL Q8_0 direct-F32 WMMA probe preserved the rejected VK128 wave64 math path and flipped only the WMMA accumulator OPSEL bit to test whether the HIP route was reading the wrong accumulator half relative to the Vulkan coopmat store/lane contract. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=22, VGPR=129, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 32 ds_load_b128, 64 global_store_b32, and 2 barriers. Focused CPU-reference gates passed for p512 and p513 candidate-selected large rows, and p33 stayed on existing narrow routes and passed, so OPSEL high is arithmetically valid for this spelling. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner focused timing regressed versus accepted BN96/BN64 packed-Q8_1 on the large rows: p512 ffn_out 8424.22 -> 9845.73 us, ffn_gate 7237.72 -> 11531.29 us, result_output 65649.00 -> 91637.90 us; p513 ffn_out 8163.48 -> 10149.92 us, ffn_gate 7480.91 -> 12667.93 us, result_output 66834.12 -> 104780.57 us. Focused p512 and p513 route traces selected this provider on the intended large Q8_0 rows, while p33 stayed on existing Q8_1 routes and passed. The selected large rows failed strict CPU-reference with finite ERR around 0.0036-0.0039. This refutes row-stream accumulation order under the selected-half output map; the pressure win cannot be promoted without either a Vulkan-equivalent numerical acceptance contract or a different live-range reduction that preserves the non-stream WMMA accumulation order.

The full-tile pack-stage selected probe preserved the non-stream WMMA issue order that passes strict correctness and removed packed input/output edge guards only for exact 128x128-aligned large rows. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=24, VGPR=193, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. This lowers the correctness-control pressure from VGPR=196 to VGPR=193 but still misses the RADV 192 ceiling and moves the store surface farther from RADV. Focused p512 CPU-reference passed with route traces selecting the candidate on ffn_out, ffn_gate, and result_output; p33 and p513 were correctly guarded out and passed on existing Q8_1 routes. Same-runner focused perf regressed versus default Q8_1 routes: ffn_out 7031.762 -> 8422.038 us, ffn_gate 6433.416 -> 7332.741 us, result_output 56130.024 -> 64645.333 us. Rejected for promotion.

The named-fragment pack-stage selected probe preserved the strict-correct non-stream A/B load-before-wait and col-then-row WMMA issue order, but spelled the eight A/B fragments as named variables instead of indexed arrays to test whether LLVM kept extra array/index live range. It compiled through CMake/Ninja to the same resource/opcode shape as the indexed selected control: wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. Rejected at compile-evidence gate because it does not move toward the RADV VGPR=192 target or change the emitted schedule.

The Q5_K BHALF packed-Q8_1 probe preserved the current MMQL128 BM128/BN128 wave64 dot issue order while storing Q8_1 RHS d/s in LDS as original half payloads and converting after shared load. The first wrapper build accidentally disabled all accumulation because the shared bquad source had no no-prefetch branch; after adding the default branch it compiled through CMake/Ninja with SGPR=49, VGPR=140, LDS=9728, no spills, wave64, and 512 v_dot4_i32_iu8. Static scoring moved footprint slightly below default but did not improve the local dot window: BHALF scored 12 pre-dot LDS loads, final lgkmcnt=1, and 54 dot ops in the first window versus default 13, 2, and 58. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates passed; route traces selected BHALF only on p512 full-tile rows, while p33 stayed on rows2_cols8 and p513 stayed on the existing MMQL tail path. Focused p512 timing was mixed with a 1.10% four-row sum win, but same-binary Qwen2.5 Coder 7B Q5_K_M p512/fa1 model A/B regressed from 455.164 to 454.457 tok/s with BHALF selected and no fallback. Rejected for gfx1151 promotion; RHS half-scale cache footprint is not the missing parity axis by itself.

The BM128/BN64 split-qsum probe retested row ownership after the accepted BN112/BN128 split-qsum routes proved that qsum live-range splitting can remove the Q8_0 register cliff. The new CMake/Ninja-built route fixed the old BM128/BN64 compile blocker, compiling with wave32, SGPR=22, VGPR=144, LDS=2176, no spills, and private segment 0. Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates all passed and route traces selected the opt-in provider. Timing rejects it versus current defaults: p512 total 72.631 ms -> 132.665 ms and p513 total 80.896 ms -> 139.952 ms, with large regressions on ffn_gate and result_output. This closes BM128/BN64 row ownership as a Q8_0 packed-path parity axis despite the fixed compile resource shape.

The pack-stage fast-half selected-output compile probe combined the correctness-proven gfx1151 wave64 D-coordinate map with the low-barrier fast-half LDS output-stage primitive, while still writing and reloading the unselected half as a dummy payload to preserve the halfword LDS opcode surface. It built through CMake/Ninja and compared against the Llama 3.1 8B Q8_0 p512 RADV large oracle with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 s_barrier. It is rejected at compile-contract gate: it does not recover RADV's VGPR=192 pressure, emits only 128 buffer_store_b32 versus RADV's 192, and serializes the first WMMA LDS load window with final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=0 and only one ds_load_b64 immediately before the final wait, while RADV keeps 59 ds_load_b64 operations outstanding with final lgkmcnt=51. The selected-half ownership rule is valid, but this HIP C++ spelling does not reproduce the Vulkan cooperative-matrix load/store schedule.

The nowait named-fragment staged-wait probe tested a precise first-WMMA issue-window hypothesis: replace the rejected nowait named-frag route's single zero wait with staged waits at lgkmcnt(12), lgkmcnt(8), lgkmcnt(4), and lgkmcnt(0) before the B-column WMMA groups. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=196, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 14 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. It is rejected at compile-contract gate because LLVM scheduled the partial waits after the first WMMA group rather than preserving a RADV-like pre-WMMA high-lgkmcnt gate: RADV scores 59 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 59 loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 22 WMMA in window; this route scores 24, 0, lgkmcnt=0, and 16 WMMA in the first-WMMA window, while still lacking the RADV halfword LDS store/load and 192 buffer-store topology.

The nowait named-fragment preuse probe added an empty inline-asm use of all eight A/B fragment vectors before the first wait, testing whether an artificial data dependency can force the fragment LDS loads to materialize before the first WMMA. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=212, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 8 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. It moved the first-WMMA score in the intended direction versus the prior nowait named-frag route, from 24 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 / 0 loads immediately before final wait / lgkmcnt=0 to 32 / 32 / lgkmcnt=0. It is rejected because RADV is still 59 / 59 / lgkmcnt=51 with VGPR=192, while this source spelling raises pressure to VGPR=212 and still lacks the RADV halfword LDS store/load and 192 buffer-store topology.

The preuse staged-wait probe combined the prior all-fragment preuse dependency with a wider staged wait ladder at lgkmcnt(24), lgkmcnt(16), lgkmcnt(8), and lgkmcnt(0), testing whether HIP C++ can keep the preuse-created 32-load window partially outstanding before the first WMMA. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=212, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 2 ds_store_b32, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 14 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. It is rejected at compile-contract gate: the nonzero waits were emitted, but the final pre-WMMA score became 32 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 0 loads immediately before the final wait, final lgkmcnt=0, and 16 WMMA in the first window. RADV remains 59 / 59 / lgkmcnt=51 / 22 WMMA with VGPR=192 and the halfword LDS plus 192-store topology.

The depwait real-fragment probe ports the accepted CMake WMMA issue-window diagnostic into the real Q8_0 direct-WMMA path by copying real A/B fragments through dependency-pinned inline asm and emitting a RADV-like wait ladder. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=28, VGPR=240, LDS=20480, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 38 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. The compile contract preserves final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=51 and the wait ladder, but the real-fragment source only presents one k_tile at a time, so the first-WMMA score is 32 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 and 32 loads immediately before the final wait rather than RADV's 59 and 59, while VGPR pressure rises to 240 versus RADV's 192. After selected-lane WMMA diagnostics proved odd accumulator halves should not veto the full 4x4 shape, the route was wired as an opt-in runtime probe and passed focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference gates. Route traces showed p33 stayed on BN64 and p512/p513 selected the depwait route only for the intended large rows. Same-runner focused timing still rejected it versus current packed-Q8_1 defaults: p512 total 71977.24 -> 101026.76 us and p513 total 81449.83 -> 116681.09 us, with the dominant large FFN/output rows regressing about 30%. Keep it as a diagnostic selector only.

The two-K-tile depwait probe forced both VK128 K tiles' A/B fragments live before the first WMMA, mechanically testing whether HIP C++ can reach RADV's 59-load pre-WMMA issue window in the real non-stream selected-half Q8_0 path. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=256, VGPR spills=30, private segment=124, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 67 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. The first-WMMA schedule score improves substantially versus the one-tile depwait route: 57 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 31 loads immediately before the final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 20 WMMAs in the first window. It is still rejected at compile-contract gate because RADV is 59/59/lgkmcnt=51 with VGPR=192 and no spills, while this HIP C++ spelling creates a hard register cliff and still lacks RADV's 128 ds_store_b16, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, and 192 buffer_store_b32 cooperative writeback topology.

The two-K-tile no-preuse depwait probe preserved the K2 source-visible A/B fragment loads and RADV-like wait ladder, but disabled the explicit empty inline-asm preuse of all 16 loaded fragments. This mechanically tested whether the K2 register cliff came from the artificial preuse dependency rather than from exposing both K tiles before the first WMMA. It built through CMake/Ninja and emitted the same tracked contract as the original K2 route: wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=256, VGPR spills=30, private segment=124, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 67 s_waitcnt, 44 s_waitcnt_depctr, first-WMMA score 57 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 31 loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 20 WMMAs in the first window. Rejected before runtime because removing the explicit preuse does not reduce pressure or improve the issue window; the live-range cliff is inherent to this source-level two-K fragment exposure.

The two-K-tile direct-wait probe preserved the K2 preload shape but removed the dependency-copy v_mov path, issuing direct WMMA calls with explicit RADV-like wait counts. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=196, no spills, private segment=0, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, and 37 s_waitcnt. This proves the K2 register cliff is caused by the dependency-copy machinery, not by the two-K source variables alone. It is still rejected at compile-contract gate because the compiler collapses the first-WMMA issue window back to 24 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, zero loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=0, and 16 WMMAs in the first window. RADV remains 59/59/lgkmcnt=51/22 with VGPR=192 and no spills.

The two-K-tile raw-fragment depwait probe preserved the K2 RADV-like wait ladder but loaded both K tiles as raw u64x4 LDS fragments, casting to half16 only at the WMMA boundary. This mechanically tested whether the K2 spill cliff was caused by the half16 vector representation rather than by exposing both K tiles and dependency-copying operands. It built through CMake/Ninja with the same tracked pressure contract as the original K2 depwait route: wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=256, VGPR spills=30, private segment=124, LDS=20480, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 buffer_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, 67 s_waitcnt, and 44 s_waitcnt_depctr. The first-WMMA score stays in the K2 neighborhood, with 57 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, 31 loads immediately before final wait, final lgkmcnt=51, and 20 WMMAs in the first window. Rejected before runtime because raw fragment representation does not reduce pressure or recover RADV's no-spill 192-VGPR contract, 59/59 issue window, or halfword LDS/writeback topology.

The B-stripe compile-contract probe preserved the accepted BM64/BN128 split-qsum route and explicitly preloaded each 16-column B-cache iqs stripe before dot consumption to test whether source-visible B issue ordering can change the packed path's first-dot schedule. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=152, LDS=4352, no spills, 512 v_dot4_i32_iu8 sites, and the exact same first-hot-op score as accepted BN128 split-qsum: 28 pre-hot loads, final lgkmcnt=14, and 60 hot ops. Rejected before runtime because it does not change the emitted schedule or resource contract; future Q8_0 packed work needs a materially different issue/window primitive or lower-level path, not local B-cache staging spelling.

DeepSeek R1 Qwen 14B Q4_K_M p512 remained below Vulkan despite accepted Q4 B-quad routing, so the embedded Q6_K prompt rows were isolated as a selector-policy probe. Exported DeepSeek Q6 rows Vcur-0, ffn_out-0, and result_output all passed CPU-reference with the current Q6 VK128 WMMA default and with the rollback path. Route traces showed the default selected hrx_mul_mat_vec_q6_k_wmma16x16_vk128_padded_w64_f16acc_wg256_f32 for all focused rows, while rollback selected rows2_cols8 for Vcur and q8_1_x4_mmql64x128 for ffn_out/result_output. Same-runner focused p512 timing rejects rollback decisively: Vcur 1450.68 -> 2939.99 us, ffn_out 24145.94 -> 198921.26 us, and result_output 292046.56 -> 2199564.33 us. The DeepSeek gap is not fixed by undoing the accepted Q6 large WMMA selector; future work should target a materially different Q6 schedule primitive or another measured boulder.

The Q5_K VK128 packstage+fast-half selected-store probe ports the Q8_0 direct-WMMA diagnostic controls into the Q5 source family: ds_write_b32 A/B pack staging, B64GROUP LDS fragment reads, selected-half LDS b16 store/load, and raw buffer stores. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=37, VGPR=199, LDS=22528, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 128 ds_load_u16_d16, 128 ds_store_b16, 128 buffer_store_b32, and 2 barriers. This mechanically reaches the RADV large-route LDS and halfword topology axes that previous Q5 bufferstore probes missed, but focused p512 CPU-reference failed on all four Q5 rows with large finite error: Kcur ERR 1.9417, Qcur ERR 3.9573, ffn_out ERR 3.9666, and ffn_gate ERR 3.8717. Route traces confirmed p33 correctly stayed on existing rows2/VK64 policy and p512 selected the candidate. Reject before perf/model testing: the selected-half accumulator store/lane mapping is not semantically valid for Q5 in this HIP C++ spelling, and the route still emits 128 rather than RADV's 192 buffer_store_b32.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 H4LOAD probe preserved the accepted p33 medium-route clone's BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64/11264-byte-LDS contract and changed LDS fragment reads from scalar half indexing to half4 chunk loads. This directly tested whether source-visible half4 reads could move the accepted narrow route toward the Qwen3 30B Q6_K p33 RADV medium topology: 16 WMMA sites, 48 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, 64 LDS b16 stores, and 96 buffer stores. It built through CMake/Ninja but is compile-equivalent to the accepted VK64 route for the tracked facts: wave64, SGPR=36, VGPR=59, LDS=11264, no spills, 8 visible v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 20 ds_load_2addr_b64, 0 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_u16_d16, 2 ds_store_b16, 16 global_store_b32, 2 s_barrier, and 58 s_waitcnt. Reject before runtime timing; this local HIP C++ load spelling does not expose the missing RADV cooperative load/store topology.

The Q6_K VK64 padded44 GROUPK2 probe changed the live fragment topology instead of just changing source load syntax: each wave preloads both K tiles' four A fragments plus one B fragment through nowait b64 LDS reads before issuing the eight WMMAs. This mechanically targeted RADV's p33 medium issue window, where 48 ds_load_b64 appear before the first WMMA with final lgkmcnt(40) and 16 WMMAs in the first window. The compile contract moved in the intended direction versus accepted VK64: wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=101, LDS=11264, no spills, 40 ds_load_b64, 8 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 16 global_store_b32, 2 barriers, 10 s_waitcnt, and 41 s_waitcnt_depctr. However, the scored first window only had 20 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, final lgkmcnt(0), and 8 WMMAs, still short of RADV. Focused p33 CPU-reference failed all three rows with NaNs while route traces confirmed GROUPK2 selection. p512 and p513 non-steal CPU-reference gates passed and stayed on the existing VK128 provider. Reject before timing/model tests; the simple grouped nowait preload is not a correct substitute for RADV's cooperative load/WMMA schedule.

The GROUPK2_WAIT probe kept GROUPK2's two-K grouped fragment topology but replaced nowait b64 fragment reads with the existing per-load wait helper to isolate whether GROUPK2's NaNs were a wait/dependency issue or a lane/fragment mapping issue. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=40, VGPR=101, LDS=11264, no spills, 40 ds_load_b64, 8 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 16 global_store_b32, 2 barriers, 50 s_waitcnt, and 41 s_waitcnt_depctr. The scored first window remained far from RADV: 20 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64, final lgkmcnt(0), and only 4 WMMAs in the first-WMMA window versus RADV's 48/lgkmcnt(40)/16. Focused p33 CPU-reference selected the route and changed the failure mode from NaNs to finite mismatch: Vcur passed, ffn_out failed with ERR 0.001619838, and result_output failed with ERR 0.007942211. p512 and p513 non-steal gates passed and stayed on VK128. Reject before timing/model testing; the missing schedule cannot be recovered by simply adding per-load waits to the grouped scalar-fragment preload.

This probe preserved the accepted Q5_K VK64 padded44 wave64 narrow FFN-gate schedule and changed only the full-tile writeback policy. It built through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=32, VGPR=75, LDS=11264, private segment=0, and no spills. Focused CPU-reference passed for p33 and p512/p513 non-steal gates; p33 route traces selected the fullstore provider only for the k=3584 rows=18944 cols=33 FFN gate/up slice, while p512/p513 stayed on rows2 plus MMQL128 routes. Initial focused timing improved ffn_gate 1797.31 -> 1758.83 us and repeated model A/B improved Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 steady tok/s 169.717 -> 171.064. However, post-edit same-runner focused timing was mixed: one pass regressed ffn_gate 1827.65 -> 1864.51 us, while the rerun improved ffn_gate 1821.96 -> 1810.51 us with noisy neighboring rows. A current-head r9 rerun kept the model-level signal small but positive, 170.072 -> 171.744 steady tok/s, and route traces confirmed 486 dispatches switched from the accepted VK64 narrow provider to fullstore. The decisive focused rerun remained flat/noisy: Kcur 71.865 -> 74.072 us, Qcur 259.392 -> 259.291 us, ffn_out 1537.784 -> 1532.410 us, and ffn_gate 1716.238 -> 1717.690 us. Reject for default promotion because the focused kernel evidence does not show a durable target-row win; keep opt-in as a diagnostic writeback-axis probe.

The Q5_K VK64 combined96 probe transplanted the standalone p33 medium fixture into the real direct-F32 Q5 wrapper as a p33-only opt-in catalog route. It built through CMake/Ninja and preserved the main RADV p33 total surface better than prior VK64 probes: wave64, LDS=11264, private segment=0, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 48 ds_load_b64, 64 ds_load_u16_d16, and 96 buffer_store_b32. However, the real ABI schedule did not preserve the fixture's issue window: static compare against RADV aligned_m showed SGPR=55 versus 108, VGPR=142 versus 144, 66 ds_store_b16 versus 64, 4 barriers versus 2, only 20 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 versus 48, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt(0) versus 40. Focused p33 CPU-reference selected the combined96 route for all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M rows and failed all four with NaNs. Reject before timing/model tests; the catalog port proves the opcode-count surface is reachable in the real ABI, but lane ownership and compiler scheduling still need a lower-level dependency/lane-mapping reproducer before another production promotion attempt.

The Q5_K VK64 full64 probe repaired the combined96 output-ownership bug by computing all 16 medium-tile output groups in wave0 and writing only groups 0..15. It built through CMake/Ninja and selected for all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 focused rows, but CPU-reference failed all four with NaNs. A follow-up CMake-built lane-map fixture, hrx-hip-bench-wmma-f16-lane-map --mode=full64-store-contract, proved the full64 coordinate contract itself is valid for cols 32, 33, and 64: all target cells were written exactly once with no NaNs. Additional CMake-built WMMA/LDS fixtures narrowed the failure: one-K, two-K, and production stride44 LDS-fed fragment probes can produce NaNs in inactive odd accumulator slots, and per-load lgkmcnt waits do not clear those inactive-slot NaNs, but the selected even output slots remain finite in the generic, long-repeat, and production-stride fixtures. A final CMake-built exact-kernel reproducer, hrx-hip-bench-q5-wmma-full64-repro, launched the actual full64 catalog kernel with synthetic Q5 dequant data and reproduced selected-output NaNs. The small-scale profile reproduced p33 NaNs with no Infs for rows=64, cols=33, k=256/512/3584, so this is not just a stress-scale F16 overflow artifact. Reduced-active-group variants using the same Q5 dequant, stride44 LDS staging, b64 fragment loads, and full64 store contract further bracketed the failure: active1 and active4 were finite, active8 was finite but badly wrong, and active12/active16 reproduced selected-output NaNs. A batched4 full-output diagnostic then computed all sixteen output groups four at a time; it was finite for the p33 small-scale case and matched the active4 error scale. Therefore the failure requires the exact Q5 dequant/shared-layout source context plus the high live-accumulator full64 topology; it is not explained by missing/duplicate output coordinates, simple LDS wait placement, or stride44 fragment loads alone. Static compare against the p33 RADV medium oracle still shows this is not a viable schedule clone: SGPR=64 versus 108, VGPR=198 versus 144, LDS=11264, no spills, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 versus 16, 64 ds_load_b64 versus 48, 64 buffer_store_b32 versus 96, no ds_load_u16_d16 store stage, 3 barriers versus 2, only 24 pre-WMMA ds_load_b64 in the scored first window, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt(0) instead of RADV lgkmcnt(40). Reject before timing/model tests; the HIP builtin/register allocation for 12+ live f16 WMMA accumulators is outside the useful schedule family. The next candidate should use low live-accumulator group batching or a closer RADV cooperative staging/writeback spelling, not a monolithic full64 accumulator set.

The Q5_K VK64 batched4 catalog probe moved the finite exact-kernel diagnostic into an opt-in p33 route: BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64, full medium-tile output ownership, but only four live f16 WMMA accumulator groups at a time. It built through CMake/Ninja; the selected batched4 export reports SGPR=51, VGPR=186, LDS=11264, private segment=0, no spills, and wavefront_size=64. The HSACO also contains the included full64 helper export, but route traces select the batched4 export by name. Focused p33 CPU-reference passed all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M rows with route evidence, proving that low live-accumulator batching avoids the full64 selected-output NaNs in the real catalog ABI. Same-runner focused timing rejects it as a production schedule: Kcur 72.754 -> 1386.552 us, Qcur 259.498 -> 1771.570 us, ffn_out 1535.251 -> 12762.069 us, and ffn_gate 1715.737 -> 8246.900 us. The selected-symbol ISA explains the loss: 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 256 ds_load_b64, 64 buffer_store_b32, and 12 barriers versus RADV p33 medium's 16 WMMA, 48 ds_load_b64, 96 buffer stores, and 2 barriers. Reject before model tests. Keep the correctness conclusion, but the next candidate must preserve low live accumulator pressure without restaging A/B four times; a closer RADV cooperative staging/writeback spelling is still required.

The Q5_K VK64 wave4row probe tested the obvious next pivot after batched4: keep BM64/BN64/BK32/WG256/wave64 and full medium-tile ownership, but map the four waves in the workgroup to the four 16-row stripes so each wave keeps only four live f16 WMMA accumulators while A/B are staged once per K tile. The initial nowait LDS fragment-load spelling selected for all focused p33 rows but failed CPU-reference with finite errors on Kcur/Qcur/ffn_gate and one NaN on ffn_out, proving the multi-wave shape needs explicit fragment-load waits. The waited spelling built through CMake/Ninja and passed all four focused Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 rows with route evidence. Its selected export reports wave64, SGPR=32, VGPR=102, LDS=11264, private segment=0, no spills, 8 visible v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 40 ds_load_b64, 16 buffer_store_b32, 2 barriers, and 51 s_waitcnt. This is the closest HIP C++ p33 medium compile contract so far, but same-runner focused timing still rejects it: Kcur 72.210 -> 398.540 us, Qcur 259.574 -> 474.473 us, ffn_out 1538.760 -> 3406.255 us, and ffn_gate 1721.514 -> 2380.085 us. Reject before model tests. The evidence says all-wave low-live WMMA can be made correct and avoids the batched4 restage explosion, but direct-F32 WMMA still loses to the accepted rows2/cols8 path; the next Q5 p33 route needs either a closer RADV cooperative store/fragment contract or a packed-Q8_1 medium schedule rather than another direct-F32 WMMA ownership reshuffle.

The Q5_K VK64 batched4-p33 probe moved the standalone p33-pruned batched4 diagnostic into an opt-in catalog route. It preserved the exact full batched4 source topology for groups 0..11 and skipped only the unused group_base=12 phase. It built through CMake/Ninja and selected for all four Qwen2.5 Coder Q5_K_M p33 focused rows. CPU-reference passed Kcur, Qcur, and ffn_gate but failed ffn_out at k=18944 rows=3584 cols=33 with finite ERR=0.043113960, so the standalone correctness result at k=256/k=3584 did not generalize to the wide-K focused row. It preserved the same BM128 no-copy inline-WMMA topology but changed the wait ladder to 24/16 for the two selected column groups. Reject before timing/model tests. This closes the simple no-copy direct-wait bracket: the correctness issue is not fixed by making the B column loads nominally ready, so the next parity probe should use a correctness-proven fragment materialization or lower-level cooperative writeback/lane-store primitive rather than another no-copy wait-count tweak.

The A-copy direct-wait bracket tested whether the correctness-clean all-wait BM128 A-copy materialization boundary could be combined with the delayed direct-wait ladder that better matches the RADV large Q8_0 issue window. It built through normal CMake/Ninja catalog HSACO generation and remained opt-in. Reject before timing/model tests. A-fragment materialization alone does not make the direct-wait ladder correct; it changes the failure mode from finite wrong values to NaNs.

The B-copy direct-wait bracket tested the fragment side most implicated by the standalone fragment-copy diagnostics: materialize the selected B fragments while preserving the BM128 phase96 direct-wait issue ladder and direct buffer-store output path. It built through normal CMake/Ninja catalog HSACO generation and stayed opt-in. Static gfx1151 codegen matched the no-copy direct-wait resource surface: each phase is wave64, SGPR=50, VGPR=163, LDS=20480, private_segment=0, no spills, 16 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 32 buffer_store_b32, two barriers, and final pre-WMMA lgkmcnt=31. Focused p513 selected B-copy for the same large rows and failed with NaNs at indices 131072, 468992, and 4114432. Reject before timing/model tests. B-fragment materialization alone does not repair the direct-wait schedule either. Together with no-copy finite errors, B-ready finite errors, and A-copy NaNs, this closes the simple BM128 direct-wait materialization bracket; the next Q8 parity probe should move to a lower-level cooperative lane/store primitive or a correctness-proven full-output ownership topology, not another selected-half wait/materialization variant.

The KTileFrag raw16 full-tile route intersected the correctness-passing raw16 full-tile writeback branch with the KTileFrag issue family, which previously had the best direct-WMMA issue surface but paid the motif192 staged halfword writeback path. The probe stayed opt-in and built through CMake/Ninja as a normal catalog HSACO. Static gfx1151 codegen was no-spill and full-tile compact: wave64, SGPR=24, VGPR=209, LDS=20480, private_segment=0, 32 v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, 64 ds_load_b64, 64 buffer_store_b32, 2 ds_store_b32, and 3 barriers. It did not reach the RADV large-route hot window: final pre-hot lgkmcnt=12 versus the Vulkan large Q8_0 route's lgkmcnt=51, with only 32 immediate LDS loads before the final wait instead of the RADV 59-load/one 32-WMMA window signature. Focused p33 and p513 guarded out and passed on existing odd/tail routes. After adding this env gate to the Q8_0 Q8_1 bypass list, focused p512 selected the candidate for ffn_out, ffn_gate, and result_output and passed CPU-reference; Vcur and Qcur correctly stayed on the accepted packed-Q8_1 route. Same-runner focused p512 perf then rejected the candidate: total 67601.646 -> 75674.303 us (0.893x), ffn_out 6719.221 -> 8109.506 us (0.829x), ffn_gate 5967.390 -> 6912.988 us (0.863x), and result_output 52561.786 -> 58264.905 us (0.902x). Reject for promotion. Combining KTileFrag issue order with compact raw16 full-tile stores preserves correctness but remains slower than the accepted packed-Q8_1 scalar-dot route; the next Q8 parity probe needs a lower-level cooperative writeback or a schedule that actually reproduces the RADV long LDS-load/wait window, not another compact full-tile store splice.

Focused p33/p512/p513 CPU-reference then passed with route evidence; p33 stayed on rows2_cols8, while p512/p513 selected motif192. Same-runner focused perf rejects production promotion: p512 improved Vcur 507.998 -> 429.316 us (1.183x) but regressed node_100 860.208 -> 1955.224 us (0.440x) and Qcur 818.377 -> 1587.288 us (0.516x); p513 improved Kcur 881.010 -> 725.227 us (1.215x) but regressed Qcur 1485.182 -> 2681.155 us (0.554x), ffn_out 8922.935 -> 17539.908 us (0.509x), and ffn_gate 8229.303 -> 15248.262 us (0.540x).
